label: prop:sw-classical-jet-exactness
title: The classical-jet prolongation of $\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}$ is exact for $n \ge 1$
html:
Let X^{(n)} denote the n-th total z-derivative of the fibre coordinate X on the colour spectral curve \Sigma of the MI--SW abelianisation, and let \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} = X^{(n)}(z)\,dz be the classical-jet prolongation of the Seiberg--Witten differential. For every n \ge 1,

\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} \;=\; d\bigl(X^{(n-1)}\bigr)

is an exact meromorphic differential on \Sigma. Consequently \mathrm{Res}_p\,\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} = 0 at every point p \in \Sigma, and \oint_\gamma \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} = 0 over every closed cycle \gamma avoiding the poles of X^{(n-1)}. In particular the residue-sum period of the SW period framework vanishes identically at every vertical degree n \ge 1 under the classical-jet rule, so the classical-jet prolongation cannot realise the nonzero binding periods a_D^{(m)} = \mathrm{lw}(m-1) = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{\lambda \vdash m} \dim_q(\lambda); the prolongation carrying the binding periods must therefore be non-classical (q-difference).

Lean structure

The load-bearing invariant is proved on the formal-residue model over a generic commutative ring: a local Laurent expansion is its coefficient function, the residue is the coefficient of t^{-1}, and a termwise derivative has vanishing t^{-1} coefficient (fresidue_fderiv). The theorem classical_jet_period_zero composes this with the residue-sum shape of prop:sw-period-residue-sum (taken as an explicit hypothesis, as in the sibling sw_period_eq_residue_sum), and classical_jet_period_ne_lw concludes against the nonzero classical binding period I(m)/m (involution numbers). Exact numerical companion at z = \infty (sheet expansions, jets n = 1\ldots4): computations/lever1_saddle_action_jet_residue_probe.py.
